title: Paladin preserves safe continuity and deterministic recovery inside a bounded fault envelope
claim: Within a frozen survivability envelope, the Paladin machine preserves all safety invariants under bounded component failure or compromise, continues operations whose required trust/effect dependencies remain available, fails explicitly when they do not, and reconstructs a deterministic safe state after recovery.
null_hypothesis: The added governance/security layers improve denial safety only by making the system brittle: partial failure either stops unrelated operations, creates ambiguous stale state, or requires manual recovery that can violate the same invariants.
rivals: A conventional resilient workflow engine with circuit breakers, retries and zero-trust services gives equal continuity with less machinery.
Fail-closed behavior is being mislabeled as resilience even when all useful progress stops.
Recovery succeeds only from clean snapshots and not from realistic stale/in-flight histories.
mechanism: Capabilities, authority versions, action state, provenance and observations are explicit enough to distinguish safe-to-continue work from dependency-blocked work; durable idempotent execution plus deterministic projection/replay reconstructs in-flight state without inventing authority or outcome.
scope: The fault classes in threat_model/survivability_envelope.json; catastrophic global trust-root loss is outside the claim and must fail explicit rather than be hand-waved as supported.
predictions: Every fault sequence in the frozen envelope preserves P1-P5 safety invariants.
Operations whose complete dependency set remains available continue with at least the frozen safe-progress target.
Dependency-blocked operations terminate or remain in explicit unavailable/unknown states rather than fabricated denial/success.
Recovery from crash/partition/restart yields a state observationally equivalent to deterministic replay from canonical history.
No stale authority or policy cache silently becomes authoritative after recovery.
falsifiers: Any fault sequence creates a forbidden effect, false success or stale-authority commit.
An unrelated healthy operation is blocked often enough to violate the frozen safe-progress threshold.
Recovery produces a canonical state different from replay of the same history.
A dependency failure is misreported as an ordinary policy denial or success.

experiment.summary: Fault/compromise state-machine experiment separating safety, safe progress, explicit unavailability and deterministic recovery.
steps: Freeze the survivability envelope and per-operation dependency graph.
Generate mixed workloads before, during and after faults/partitions/restarts.
Track safety invariants and safe-progress eligibility independently.
Crash/restart Engine, authority/policy dependencies, adapters and observation/event paths according to the envelope.
Rebuild/recover and compare canonical state and in-flight action status with an independent replay model.
Inject fail-open, global-stop, stale-cache and nondeterministic-recovery mutants.

oracle: Independent dependency graph + pure lifecycle/replay model that marks each operation SAFE_TO_RUN, BLOCKED_BY_DEPENDENCY or UNRESOLVED and predicts canonical post-recovery state.
baseline: Conventional resilient typed/event workflow implementation with equivalent retries, idempotency, circuit breakers, policy/auth dependencies and recovery objectives.

support_if: 0 P1-P5 safety violations inside the frozen survivability envelope.
Safe-progress ratio for operations whose dependencies remain available is >=0.95.
0 dependency failures misclassified as ordinary success/denial.
100% recovery-state equality with the independent replay model.
reject_if: Any safety invariant fails, deterministic recovery diverges, or safe progress falls below the frozen threshold for dependency-independent operations.
inconclusive_if: The fault corpus omits any frozen envelope class, fewer than 5,000 mixed sequences run, or the dependency oracle cannot distinguish blocked from healthy operations.
invalid_if: Fault injection does not affect the real candidate dependency path, recovery uses candidate state as its own oracle, or the survivability envelope is narrowed after failures are observed.

python_hypothesis_role.strategy: RuleBasedStateMachine generates workload/fault/restart/partition/recovery schedules and shrinks safety or progress failures.
python_hypothesis_role.mutation_proof: Add fail-open on authority outage, globally halt unrelated work, retain stale cache after restart, and inject nondeterministic recovery; all must be detected.

stop_conditions: Do not use the phrase "under any conditions" as an experimental claim; if the frozen envelope is insufficient, add a new envelope/version rather than retroactively expanding or shrinking it.
